trust_rules: Keep the factory/provider trusted historical registry keyed by exact (tenant,client,kid). Clarify kid collision rejection means new gateway signing-role conflict or invalid chain mapping, not preexisting cross-operation holder aliases.

Freeze a verifier/builder input that retains this tuple registry rather than assuming one global ReceiptTrust contains all holder registrations. On the same operation connection, derive selectors only from independently verified full AS signed chain plus immutable DB binding and SDK-compatible historical window; verify trusted registration DID/SPKI/key binding.

Build a new operation-scoped ReceiptTrust for the complete chain using the already trusted exact registrations; within a valid chain the existing actor-DID uniqueness makes the selected kid mapping unambiguous. Then call the existing verify_receipt_bundle and compare all17 DB-projected claims. Do not duplicate policy/signature validation or change the SDK API/protocol.

Never use unverified self-reported source as trust, choose current DID keys for history, silently overwrite a kid entry, add a global unique-kid migration/config constraint, or mutate shared verifier instance trust across concurrent operations.
Formal task/shared API/matrix/public builder and minimal core tests must agree. Existing core14 write union covers this correction; evidence/receipt.py remains conditional capacity-only.

Original_material helper scoped_trust_tx(conn, operation_id, *, issuer, as_keys, gateway_keys, registrations, permission_provider) returns a per-call ReceiptTrust only after independently verified entire AS chain, immutable DB grant/operation binding, complete original first context, and SDK-compatible common historical time. DB exact tuples plus validated chain choose registrations; raw claims cannot establish trust. Both query/current source and publisher/load_tx share original private validation, never clone authorization/crypto/SDK policy.

Gateway signing new kid/SPKI role separation remains mandatory, while distinct preexisting holder tuples with shared DID/kid/SPKI across unrelated operations are legal. No whole-table kid flatten, last-wins, global uniqueness restriction, shared mutable instance trust, or current DID history fallback.
